result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_non_neighbors()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get nodes that are NOT neighbors of the specified node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5014-L5075){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_non_neighbors(node) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns all nodes in the graph except the specified node itself and its neighbors. Useful for finding potential new connections or disconnected nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node ID or label to find non-neighbors for. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Sorted list of node IDs that are not neighbors of `node=` and are not `node=` itself. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In this 5-node path, node `2` connects only to `1` and `3`, so everything else -- `4` and `5` -- comes back as a non-neighbor: ::: {#b719c729 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_path_graph(5) # 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 graph.get_non_neighbors(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [4, 5] ``` ::: ::: This makes a useful candidate pool for recommending new connections -- for example, ranking candidates by how many neighbors they already share with the target node: ::: {#c9ee5550 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") ) node_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") candidates = graph.get_non_neighbors(node_id) [(candidate, len(graph.get_common_neighbors(node_id, candidate))) for candidate in candidates] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [(3, 1), (4, 0)] ``` ::: :::
